Order
% 22.03.2023 Crl.M.A.6260/2023 (for exemption)
1. Exemption allowed, subject to just exceptions.
2. The application stands disposed of.

3. The instant writ petition under Article 226 of Constitution of India read with Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 ('Cr.P.C') has been filed by the petitioner praying for quashing of FIR bearing no. 0119/2019, under Sections 498-A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC),
registered at Police Station Vijay Vihar, Delhi district North-West; and subsequent proceedings arising thereupon.
4.
Mr.Satish Kumar, learned APP accepts notice on behalf of the State.

5. Petitioner is present before this Court and has been identified by his learned counsel Mr.Anil Bhargav and Investigating Officer (IO) Sub- Inspector Saurabh Malik from Police Station Vijay Vihar, Delhi.
6. Briefly stated, facts of the present case are that Petitioner No.1 was married to the Respondent No.2 as per Hindu rites and ceremonies.
The parties started living separately since 2018.
FIR was registered under Sections 498-A/406/34 IPC at PS Vijay Vihar.

It is further stated that the parties entered into a settlement before Family Court, Rohini and the Mutual Divorce Petition under Section 13 (B) (1) of Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 (HMA) for dissolution of marriage by mutual consent was allowed.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the complainant states that she entered into compromise out of her own free will and without any pressure, coercion or threat.
It is also stated that the entire dispute has been amicably settled between the parties vide Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) dated 24.03.2022 before Family Court, Rohini.

8. It is submitted that complainant has settled all her claims in respect of her dowry articles,
stridhan, marriage expenses, jewellery, gift items and claims of past, present and future maintenance and permanent alimony with petitioner.

9. The petitioner had to pay a sum of Rs. 3,50,000/- in two installments in the following manner:
a. First installment of Rs. 3,00,000/- paid to complainant at the time of recording of statement in second motion. b. Second/final instalment of Rs.50,000/- to be paid to the complainant at the time of quashing of FIR before Hon'ble High Court at New Delhi.
10.

Today, the complainant who is present in Court states that she has received the last and final instalment of Rs. 50,000/- vide DD No. 514465 dated 24.02.2023 drawn on ICICI Bank, New Delhi,
and has no objection if the FIR is quashed.

11. In view of the above facts that the parties have amicably resolved their differences out of their own free will, and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings, rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
It is in interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
There is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR.

12. Accordingly, FIR bearing no. 0119/2019, under Sections 498- A/406/34 of the IPC, registered PS Vijay Vihar, Delhi district North-West for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of the IPC and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
13. The present petition stands disposed of.
14. The order be uploaded on the website forthwith.

SWARANA KANTA SHARMA, J.
MARCH 22, 2023 neelam
